headline: Tk 9.38 trillion national budget passed in Parliament for FY2026–27
summary: The budget, effective from July 1, focuses on a 'Democratic, Humane and Inclusive Economy' with a significant increase in development expenditure.
details: Bangladesh's Parliament has approved a Tk 9.38 trillion national budget for the 2026–27 fiscal year. The budget was passed through the Appropriation Bill, 2026, and will come into effect on July 1.

The proposed expenditure is 19 percent higher than the revised budget for FY2025–26 and represents 13.73 percent of the country's GDP. Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury unveiled the plan under the theme 'Journey Towards a Democratic, Humane and Inclusive Economy'.

A major shift in spending is planned, with development expenditure increasing from 27.27 percent to 33.70 percent of the total budget. This includes Tk 3.16 trillion for development, a 47 percent increase over the previous year's revised budget.

The government has set a revenue target of Tk 6.95 trillion, an 18 percent increase from the previous year. The National Board of Revenue (NBR) is tasked with collecting Tk 6.04 trillion, with VAT expected to be the largest source at Tk 2.29 trillion.
Operating expenditure is set at Tk 6.05 trillion. This includes Tk 1.27 trillion for debt interest payments and at least Tk 893.8 billion for government employee salaries and allowances.

The budget process saw 43 lawmakers submit 1,343 cut motions. However, the Leader of the Opposition, Shafiqur Rahman, proposed withdrawing all cut motions as a package to save time, which was accepted by the Treasury Bench.

A major shift in spending is planned, with development expenditure increasing from 27.27 percent to 33.70 percent of the total budget. This includes Tk 3.16 trillion for development, a 47 percent increase over the previous year's revised budget.

The government has set a revenue target of Tk 6.95 trillion, an 18 percent increase from the previous year. The National Board of Revenue (NBR) is tasked with collecting Tk 6.04 trillion, with VAT expected to be the largest source at Tk 2.29 trillion.

Operating expenditure is set at Tk 6.05 trillion. This includes Tk 1.27 trillion for debt interest payments and at least Tk 893.8 billion for government employee salaries and allowances.

The budget process saw 43 lawmakers submit 1,343 cut motions. However, the Leader of the Opposition, Shafiqur Rahman, proposed withdrawing all cut motions as a package to save time, which was accepted by the Treasury Bench.

headline: Barishal police officer show-caused for using AI to alter suspect's jersey
summary: A sub-inspector used artificial intelligence to change an arrested drug dealer's Argentina jersey to a Brazil jersey in a photo distributed to the press.
details: A sub-inspector of the Barishal Metropolitan Police (BMP) has been served a show-cause notice after using artificial intelligence to digitally alter the image of an arrested suspect.
The officer, SI Tanzil Ahmed, was removed from his responsibility for operating the BMP media WhatsApp group after the incident was discovered.
The suspect, Russell Hawlader, was arrested on Monday afternoon in Barishal city with 800 yaba tablets in his possession.
At the time of arrest, Hawlader was wearing an Argentina jersey. Police initially turned the jersey inside out for the photograph, but SI Tanzil later used AI to replace it with a Brazil jersey.
The edited image was then circulated to journalists via email and the BMP media WhatsApp group.
Following social media criticism, the BMP corrected the image and redistributed the original photo with accurate information.
BMP Commissioner Md Ashik Sayeed stated that SI Tanzil admitted to the altering the image, claiming he did it to generate public attention and discussion during the World Cup excitement.
Tanzil has been asked to explain his actions within three days, and further action will be follow after reviewing his response.
caption:
A police officer used AI to change a suspect's football jersey in a press photo. Why?

A sub-inspector of the Barishal Metropolitan Police (BMP) has been served a show-cause notice after using artificial intelligence to digitally alter the image of an arrested suspect.

The officer, SI Tanzil Ahmed, was removed from his responsibility for operating the BMP media WhatsApp group after the incident was discovered.

The suspect, Russell Hawlader, was arrested on Monday afternoon in Barishal city with 800 yaba tablets in his possession.

At the time of arrest, Hawlader was wearing an Argentina jersey. Police initially turned the jersey inside out for the photograph, but SI Tanzil later used AI to replace it with a Brazil jersey.

The edited image was then circulated to journalists via email and the BMP media WhatsApp group.

Following social media criticism, the BMP corrected the image and redistributed the original photo with accurate information.

BMP Commissioner Md Ashik Sayeed stated that SI Tanzil admitted to the altering the image, claiming he did it to generate public attention and discussion during the World Cup excitement.

Tanzil has been asked to explain his actions within three days, and further action will be follow after reviewing his response.
